sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1. Rule.
Learned APP waives service of notice of Rule on behalf of respondent-State.

2. This application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for regular bail in connection with F.I.R. No.11191028230243 of 2023 registered with Vejalpur Police Station, District Ahmedabad, for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(3), 354(A) and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 3(a), 4, 7, 8 and 17 of the POCSO Act.
3. Learned advocate for the applicant submits that investigation is over and Charge-sheet is also filed.

He further submits that considering the nature of offence and role attributed to the applicant,
the applicant may NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/10697/2023 ORDER DATED: 19/10/2023 undefined be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.

sentences.text: Learned advocate Ms. P. J. Joshi appearing for the original complainant strongly opposes the present application inter-alia stating that there was no love affair between the present applicant and prosecutrix and the applicant has forced the prosecutrix and offence has committed.
She also submits that at that point of time when the incident taken place, the prosecutrix aged of 16 years and she was studying in 10 th standard and therefore, FIR could not be lodged.
She therefore submits that looking to the age of the prosecutrix and allegations levelled against the present applicant, the present application may not be allowed.

5. The learned APP appearing for the respondent State vehemently submits that looking to the age of prosecutrix, which was 15 years at that relevant point of time and the offences which have been charged, are serious in nature and looking to the facts as well as the allegations made against the applicant, no discretion would be required to be exercised.
5. I have heard learned advocates appearing for the parties and perused the papers of investigation.
From the record it appears that the investigation is over and Charge-sheet has already been filed.

It appears from the papers that the incident had taken place in September, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/10697/2023 ORDER DATED: 19/10/2023 undefined 2021 whereas the FIR came to be lodged belatedly on 06.04.2023 almost after a period of one and half year.
The delay in filing FIR is sought to be explained by stating that the prosecutrix appeared in 10 th standard examination so she had chosen not to lodge FIR.
The explanation given does not appear to be plausible.

The record also indicates that the maternal aunt had taken the prosecutrix to the present applicant and thereafter,
the prosecturix and the present applicant had gone to some other place where physical relation was established with consent of prosecutrix.
Considering these aspects, the present application deserves to be allowed.

6. In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of allegations made in the FIR and without discussing the evidence in details as well as without going into details, prima-facie,
this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion to enlarge the applicant on bail.
